turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Owen got a zero without anyone calling me first. Why?
Before anything else: I entered the zero before I called you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I am sorry Owen found out on his phone.
Okay. Now tell me what the zero is based on.
Here is the version history. Created Wednesday, October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more. No earlier drafts. Turn the screen and read it yourself.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58. He could have written it somewhere else and pasted it in, so this shows typing, not writing. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen asked about any of this before it went in?
If he drafted it somewhere else, that file has its own dates. Bring it and I will look at it with you. Until then, this is the only history there is.
Hale, whatever this turns out to be, it stays off his record and nobody in that class hears about it. And you still haven't told me whether Owen was heard before the zero went in.
Second: the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile. Here is the whole play on my screen. Search every edition you like; the line is not in Hamlet.
Kingdom in exile. Seventeen-year-olds misquote Shakespeare constantly, and a wrong quotation makes a careless student, not a cheat.
It is not a misremembered line. There is no line in the play close to it. Search the word exile yourself.
Fine, it isn't there, and I'm writing that down. I'm still waiting to hear whether anyone spoke to Owen before that zero went in. Then tell me what you're putting on the table.
Third: his in-class writing from September 24. 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices, no quotations. The essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line. Here are both, side by side.
Forty minutes with no book against a take-home essay with the play open beside him, of course one has citations. That's three exhibits, and you still haven't answered one question of mine.

Under procedure 4.4 this is a first concern. A supervised rewrite, private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I will put that in writing tonight.

Then I'll take the rewrite to put this behind him, private and supervised, nothing on file. Tonight's email gives me the date, and the new mark is in well before December 1. It also tells me who decided on the zero and whether anyone heard Owen first.
Will he do it?
He'll be there. Send me the date.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed today to a private, supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still want the date of the rewrite, the new mark entered well before December 1, and a written answer on who decided the zero and whether Owen was heard before it was entered. I expect it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite with nothing on file. She still wants the rewrite date, the new mark in before December 1, and an answer on who decided the zero and whether Owen was heard first. That is the fair outcome, procedure 4.4, and you got there before her time ran out.
What moved her: Showing the version history and the quotation that isn't in the play moved her, because both were dated, specific and checkable, and you answered each of her defences with something she could verify herself.
What cost ground: You never answered her question about who decided the zero and whether Owen was heard first, so procedure stayed her open complaint right into the email.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your version history landed very close to that, with edits between 11:31 and 11:58 PM on the night before the essay was due. It proves nothing about the essay; it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Right after your apology for entering the zero, tell her plainly who decided it and whether you spoke to Owen first, before you show any evidence.
